summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of atrial fibrillation, diastolic heart failure, moderate aortic stenosis with regurgitation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for worsening muscle twitching and lethargy. He had a recent episode of dark emesis and was found to have uremia with elevated creatinine and BUN, hyponatremia, and a supratherapeutic INR. The twitching was attributed to uremia secondary to poor forward flow from heart failure. He was treated with IV diuresis, which improved his kidney function, resolved his asterixis, and stabilized his electrolytes. His INR was corrected with vitamin K, followed by bridging with heparin and restarting warfarin at a lower dose. Pulmonary edema was managed with increased furosemide, and he was transitioned to 40 mg daily at discharge. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged to extended care with a cardiology follow-up, daily weight monitoring, and instructions on fluid and sodium restriction.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
